study.question: At the stronger joint model and fixed pi/4 nuisance-exclusion angle, does the transported auxiliary orientation bit provide a click-AUC advantage that an explicitly click-derived bit cannot reproduce? Is bit source involved in the external-sign response after scalar auxiliary angle has been replaced?
study.hypothesis: OBSERVED, single frozen seed: initial joint click AUC 0.668457307890924 versus click-only/aux-context-blocked 0.6678548720585206 and rolled auxiliary labels 0.6674639465810746. Thus shared auxiliary context updates may matter, but generic optimization and label alignment remain competing explanations. In g3-r0057, native-angle auxiliary-bit negative/positive AUCs were 0.6689064289769298/0.6679524177535937; click-bit alternatives were 0.6687816886751912/0.6681420598160617. In g3-r0058, fixed-angle auxiliary-bit negative/positive reached 0.6689610675617089/0.6683760511656333. Latest g3-r0059 auxiliary-bit bridges replayed those values exactly, whereas canonical bit removal gave 0.6687531802698141/0.6687682991939847: the negative-minus-positive gap changed from +0.0005850163960756 to -0.0000151189241706. This is controlled outcome evidence about a surrogate selection, with tensor diagnostics absent; it does not prove useful auxiliary semantics. PROVISIONAL: auxiliary-derived s(Q) supplies a state-dependent orientation schedule beyond generic centered-click sign. At fixed angle, replacing s(Q) by s(K) should reduce the negative-cell advantage and alter the negative-minus-positive gap. Earlier canonicalization on a different line (g3-r0053 positive 0.6686452072782969, negative 0.6683159780375061) and precision-sensitive collection branches (g3-r0039-centered_replay 0.6676314512972833; g3-r0041 task32 0.6674577109894665 versus task64 0.6682972490126902) caution against transferring sign effects across geometry/precision. No trajectory failure is erased and no single failed variant refutes all auxiliary supervision.

study.proposed_difference: Add only _centered_click_orientation_bit: center occupied-row click cotangent K in FP64; choose the first maximal-absolute flattened coordinate and its sign, with exact zero assigned +1. Let D be the inherited oriented pi/4 output and U=canonical(D), including its exact zero support and radius. New positive transfer is s(K)*U; new negative transfer is its negation. Auxiliary-bit controls select D/-D exactly as before. All helpers execute in every cell; no new module, parameter, buffer, RNG, extra forward/backward evaluation, label access in forward or data lookup is introduced. At a common state, replacing the bit only globally reverses or preserves U; the custom VJP adds selected transfer to the original click cotangent before the inherited cast/scatter boundary. Architecture/method originality remains UNVERIFIED. Authorized searches for gradient surgery, PCGrad and multitask primary text returned no matching source; do not import an unavailable source or interpret access failure as scientific counterevidence. No industry card was newly retrieved or adopted in this round.
predictions: Common-state tensor preflight on host: auxiliary/click-bit variants have identical logits and all model buffers; private parameter gradients agree, and shared-context custom VJP matches the stated formula. The only new output can be D or -D before cast. Compare with surrogate formula rather than an ordinary scalar-loss finite-difference gradcheck.

The two auxiliary-bit bridges replay g3-r0059 retained negative/positive controls within a predeclared absolute AUC tolerance 1e-6 under deterministic host execution. Any larger discrepancy suspends causal interpretation pending diagnosis; do not loosen this tolerance after seeing results.

Directional screening prediction: auxiliary-bit negative AUC exceeds click-bit negative AUC; the bit-source x sign interaction I=(A_aux_neg-A_aux_pos)-(A_click_neg-A_click_pos) is positive. Treat 1e-4 absolute AUC as a practical screening scale for each contrast, not a significance threshold; report raw differences even below it.

Record full-population click AUC/logloss, all four task AUC/logloss, auxiliary mean separately, inherited history slices with sample/positive/negative counts, parameter count, allocated GPU seconds, wall time, examples processed, peak memory and inference throughput/p50/p95. No inference computation is added by the training-only bit helper, but actual speed equivalence must be measured.

Host admissibility diagnostics before interpreting mechanism: occupied/empty and inherited-zero counts; D and new output support equality and norm ratio; centered-row mean residual and K dot-transfer before/after cast; s(K)/s(Q) sign balance, agreement, pivot ties/near ties and zero-K frequency by training interval; common-state forward/buffer/private-gradient parity. These diagnostics are requested, not claimed as executed, and consume budget.
falsifiers: If the click-bit negative cell matches/exceeds the auxiliary-bit negative cell and the sign-response interaction is no larger than the predeclared 1e-4 screening scale, this experiment does not support necessity of the auxiliary-derived bit. Matching a sign gap alone would not establish useful auxiliary supervision.

If only the positive cell changes or both replacements improve, reject the stated directional prediction and retain the observed interaction without redefining success retrospectively. If all differences are small, record a null single-seed contrast.

Bridge AUC drift above 1e-6, any unexpected common-state forward/state/private-gradient difference, nonfinite cotangents, extra support loss or non-sign-only norm change invalidates the proposed attribution. Diagnose through the host interface and charge failures/retries; no training-protocol edits.

Even a positive interaction cannot identify semantics rather than different marginal/temporal sign schedules. Without tensor diagnostics and independent host-authorized repetitions, describe results as preliminary local outcome contrasts; never repeated mechanism support or holdout confirmation.
alternative_explanations: Different bits can have different marginal sign balance and temporal autocorrelation. This replacement cannot distinguish auxiliary semantic information from a favorable coordinate-based sign schedule; record both bits and their agreement/balance by training interval.
